verses.1: He ruled for forty-five years. He also ruled in Jerusalem for forty-nine years. His mother’s name was Jehoaddan from Jerusalem.
verses.2: And the righteous did what was right in the eyes of Jehovah, but not with full heart.
verses.3: And when the queen became stronger over him, she killed his servants who had killed his father.
verses.4: And they did not kill their children, because it is written in the Torah, in Moses’ book, that Jehovah commanded: “Do not kill fathers, nor may children kill their fathers. For anyone who dies in sin will die.”
verses.5: And Amasya took the Jews and gathered them together in the house of their ancestors. He made them priests for the armies of the nations, and for all the Jews. In Benjamin, he appointed them to serve for forty years. But they were found to be three hundred thousand in number. They were led by a leader named Romach and Zinah.
verses.6: And he hired from Israel ten thousand soldiers, each worth one silver shekel.
verses.7: And the man of God came to him and said, “The king of Israel will not come with you. The army of Israel will not go with you, because Jehovah is not with Israel. All the children of Ephraim are against you.”
verses.8: For if you go into battle, God will defeat you before your enemies. For God has the power to do so.
verses.9: And Amaziah said to the man of God, “What shall I do with the chest that I have been given to guard for Israel?” The man of God replied, “The LORD will give you many such chests.”
verses.10: And Amasya distinguished them, so that those who came to him from Ephraim could go to their place. He punished them greatly in Judah, and they returned to their place.
verses.11: And Amaziah became stronger. He ruled over his people. He went to the land of Elam and destroyed twelve thousand of their men.
verses.12: And twelve thousand people returned from the land of Judah. They brought them to the top of the rock, and they were thrown down from the top of the rock. And all of them died.
verses.13: And the sons of Gedaliah, who had brought Amasya back from her reign over Judah to fight against them. They conquered the cities of Judah, from Smaron to Beth Horon. They killed three thousand people from those cities.
verses.14: And after Amaziah came out from the battle against the Edomites, he brought the gods of the sons of Zephon before him. He made them stand before God. They would bow down before them, and they would offer sacrifices to them.
verses.15: And Jehovah struck Amasya, and he sent a prophet to him. The prophet said to him, “Why did you seek the help of the gods of that people, who did not save their own people from your hands?”
verses.16: And when he spoke to him, he said to him, “Hear these words from the king: ‘For what purpose do you continue to do this?’ Then the prophet stopped and said, “I know that God has commanded you to be destroyed, because you have done this. But you did not listen to my advice.”
verses.17: And Amaziah, king of Judah, sent Yoash, son of Jehoahaz, king of Israel, with a message saying, “Let us see what happens.”
verses.18: And Joash, the king of Israel, sent a message to Amaziah, the king of Judah, saying, “The woman who is from Bethlehem has sent her daughter to be married to Beni. Go and take that woman away from there.” Then Amaziah went and took the woman away from Bethlehem.
verses.19: You said, “Look, you have taken Adam and carried him away. Now, you should rest in your home. Why do you want to do evil? You will fall, along with Judah.”
verses.20: And Amaziah did not hear this, because it came from God. They wanted to have control over God of Edom.
verses.21: And Joash, the king of Israel, went up. His face was turned pale, and Jehoshaphat, the king of Judah, saw him at the house of Shem.
verses.22: And Judah was defeated before Israel. And each man went back to his own tent.
verses.23: And Amaziah, king of Judah, son of Joash, son of Jehoahaz, was captured by Joash, king of Israel, in the house of Shechem. He was brought to Jerusalem, and from the gate of Ephraim to the gate of Ben-Hadad, four miles were broken into pieces.
verses.24: And all the gold and silver, and all the utensils that were found in the Temple of God, along with the treasures of the king’s house, and all the goods of the nobles. Shushan sat on those treasures.
verses.25: Amasya, son of Joash, became king of Judah after the death of Joash, son of Jehoahaz, who was king of Israel. He ruled for fifteen years.
verses.26: And the additional words of Amasias, both the earlier and later ones, are not written in the register of the kings of Judah and Israel.
verses.27: And from the time when Amaziah was removed from his throne by Jehovah, they put a chain around him in Jerusalem. They then sent his followers to Kishah, and they killed him there.
verses.28: And they put him on the horses, and they buried him along with his ancestors in the city of Judea.
